notes.title: Rally Mechanic Simulator: LIGHT EDITION – The Updated and Expanded Prologue
notes.content:
Hey Mechanics! 🔧

Over the past months, we’ve received tons of amazing feedback about the RMS Prologue. Many of you enjoyed it, but also pointed out that it lacked some of the features that make Rally Mechanic Simulator truly special. We heard you, and we agree!
That’s why we’re taking a big step forward:

Next week, we plan to eveolve the Prologue into Rally Mechanic Simulator: LIGHT EDITION and it will remain 100% free.

This isn’t just a name change. It’s a full overhaul designed to bring the Prologue much closer to the full version of the game. We’re adding more content, more functionality, and features the community asked for - including the ability to save your game.

We want this to be a better entry point for new players, and a genuine thank-you to everyone who gave the Prologue a try. It’s our way of saying: we appreciate your support, and we want you to have fun even if you’re not ready to buy the full game yet.

🛠️ What’s coming in Rally Mechanic Simulator: LIGHT?
Here’s what you’ll get in the upcoming update:

✅ The game can now be saved!
Yes - finally! You’ll be able to continue your work between sessions, just like in the full version.

✅ All updates and bug fixes from the full version
The LIGHT edition will be upgraded to the current stable build of RMS, including performance improvements, UI fixes, and core stability enhancements.

✅ 2 free rally cars unlocked: Pudro 276 and Sortes SC95T1
These two vehicles will be fully playable, letting you experience core systems like damage handling, part swapping, diagnostics, and driving.

✅ Full access to the Paint Shop
Customize your ride just like in the full game - from base colors to decal placement and liveries.

✅ Test Drive mode with latest improvements
Take your cars for a spin before hitting the stages to test handling, upgrades, and reliability.

✅ Updated failure system
Experience realistic part breakdowns that vary based on your repairs and rally conditions.

✅ Bronze League rally access (limited)
Try a selection of beginner rally events and see how your preparation and repairs hold up under pressure.

✅ New commentator voice lines
The improved commentator system brings more atmosphere and energy to your rally events.

✅ 2 garage slots
Keep and manage multiple cars at once - just like a real rally team would!

✅ Ability to purchase extra cars via low-cost DLCs
Want to grow your garage even more? Optional car DLCs let you expand your collection at your own pace.

🚫 What’s not included in LIGHT?
To keep things balanced, some premium features will still be exclusive to the full version:
❌ No access to the Dyno
❌ No sponsorship contracts
❌ No internal tuning parts
But for a free version, we think it’s pretty packed with features! 

🏁 Why Go Full?
The full version of Rally Mechanic Simulator offers:

 A full roster of vehicles
 Advanced diagnostics, tuning, and full car management systems
 Sponsorship contracts and career progression
 More tools, upgrades, and customization options
 Deeper rally content, new environments, and ongoing updates!

We hope this change makes it easier and more fun for everyone to explore what RMS has to offer. Whether you're a newcomer, a curious player, or someone on the fence about upgrading, LIGHT EDITION is our way of making Rally Mechanic Simulator more accessible, transparent, and enjoyable for all. And if you’re loving your time in the LIGHT EDITION, upgrading is the best way to dive deeper into the world of rally mechanics.

More news soon as we roll out the update next week!

notes.title: Sponsorship Contracts Are Here! 🏁💰
notes.content:
Hey Mechanics! 🛠️

It’s time to take your rally career to the next level! Sponsorship Contracts are now live in Rally Mechanic Simulator!

This new system brings extra challenges from sponsors, allowing you to earn additional rewards while competing in rallies. Your performance on the track will now have even greater stakes, as sponsors will expect you to meet their specific requirements to secure funding!

How does it work?

🔹 Check Available Contracts – Open the Contracts tab on your laptop to browse available sponsorship deals. Each contract comes with different objectives and rewards, so choose wisely!

🔹 Monitor Your Progress – Keep track of your contract’s requirements to ensure you’re on track to complete them. Whether it’s parts-based goals, car condition or colour, sponsors will have their demands!

🔹 Cancel Contracts Anytime – If you decide a contract isn’t working out, you can cancel it anytime. Depending on your progress, you may still receive a partial payout instead of losing everything.

🔹 Complete & Get Paid! – Once you fulfill all the sponsor’s requirements, you can finalize the contract and claim your full reward. After that, you’re free to pick another deal and keep pushing your team to success!

This system adds a new layer of strategy to Rally Mechanic Simulator. Now, you’re not just fixing cars! You’re managing your career, making financial decisions, and working towards bigger rewards. Picking the right contracts at the right time can make a huge difference in your journey to the top!

Check out our video to see how it works! 👇
https://youtu.be/JsddjzWb5Ug

We’re always working on new features, improvements, and updates based on your feedback. Let us know what you think about Sponsorship Contracts and what else you'd love to see in the game!

notes.title: Devlog #15 – Finding the Perfect Balance Between Realism and Fun 👌
notes.content:
Hello Mechanics!
When creating the Rally Mechanic Simulator, we set out to capture the excitement and intensity of rally racing through the eyes of a mechanic. The challenge? Striking the perfect balance between realism and accessibility. While we wanted to deliver an authentic experience of working on rally cars, it was equally important to make the gameplay enjoyable and engaging for everyone.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/40984c1f0c514c305e41843eae5a91e67877ce9a.png

One of the key challenges we faced was translating the complex world of car repairs into a fun and approachable gameplay experience. Working on real rally cars involves various tools, technical knowledge, and detailed procedures. For the Rally Mechanic Simulator, we focused on the most satisfying aspects—unscrewing bolts, swapping parts, and seeing immediate progress.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/867f9cddd4319d8ee93c3ca8a87349b6375696e8.gif

Imagine hunting for the perfect wrench size or aligning timing belts during a race—it might be realistic, but it wouldn’t be fun. By simplifying these elements, we aimed to recreate the feeling of being a rally mechanic without overwhelming players. It’s all about maintaining the excitement while keeping things accessible.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/18fee74b9f3595b50bde80a031fedd98c21bd383.gif

At the same time, we worked hard to capture the high-stakes atmosphere of real-life rally events. Inspired by the fast-paced world of WRC, we looked closely at how mechanics operate in tents during races. Their ability to assess damage quickly, prioritize repairs, and get cars back on track greatly influenced the gameplay design.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/e361f09d1b66b48701a3260717957bd1ee53f84d.png

From the very beginning, our goal was to make the game appealing to a wide range of players, from casual gamers to hardcore rally fans. To achieve this, we introduced different difficulty levels:

 Easy Mode: Tailored for newcomers, this mode provides clear diagnostics and straightforward repair tasks, letting players focus on the fun of fixing cars.

 Hard Mode: For seasoned players and car enthusiasts, this mode ramps up the challenge by requiring players to diagnose issues themselves. Drivers offer only vague hints, and players must rely on their skills and intuition.

This approach ensures that everyone can find a level of challenge that suits their style while still enjoying the thrill of rally mechanics.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/845121a19dfbd2100ca448fc5da43b2944101cb0.gif

We also paid close attention to the details of the cars themselves. Every vehicle in the game features intricate elements like wires, tubes, and authentic part designs. These visual details enhance immersion, giving players the satisfaction of working on beautifully crafted machines while keeping the gameplay accessible.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/10258568308966d2d4bd730db8bf20646da51e5f.gif

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/c9239ed4508f69b20d6ded9d1ff3d82a129f0799.png

Beyond the repairs, we wanted to immerse players in the authentic workflow of rally mechanics. The garage serves as the heart of your operations, a space where precision and preparation make all the difference. From diagnostic areas to specialized workstations, every part of the garage is designed to give players the tools they need to fine-tune vehicles for upcoming championships.
Before each event, you’ll have the opportunity to assess the condition of the car, analyze potential weaknesses, and make adjustments to ensure peak performance on the track. Whether it’s fine-tuning the suspension, replacing worn-out parts, or optimizing the engine, the preparation phase is just as critical as the repairs themselves.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/e9d108c51c9cf5b3dd5218efdf882baeb713caab.gif

By focusing on these elements, we struck a balance between realism and fun. The result is a game that not only delivers the satisfaction of repairing cars but also captures the strategic thinking and attention to detail that define the high-stakes world of rally mechanics.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/093040555a88af0fbaef999c0f456841aef23f92.png

What do you think of our approach to balancing realism and fun? Let us know in the comments or on our social channels! Your feedback helps us continue refining the game and creating the ultimate rally mechanic experience.
Thanks for reading, and see you in the garage! 🚗💨

notes.title: Devlog #14 - The most important PART (let's talk about PARTS) 🛠️
notes.content:
Hello Mechanics!
When it comes to Rally Mechanic Simulator, it’s all about the details. Creating realistic car parts is the core of our game, and today we’re excited to take you behind the scenes to show how we bring those parts to life—from the first concept to the final 3D model.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/e3c4fef430ee7f4940fbb4bc4a37a6a5743decd8.png

Every car part starts with thorough research. Our artists dive into photos, technical drawings, and real-life examples to understand the exact shapes, sizes, and materials needed. This stage is crucial for understanding shapes, sizes, and materials. Using tools like Blender, Maya, and Substance 3D Painter, we craft each part step-by-step, paying close attention to how light interacts with different surfaces, ensuring every bolt, screw, and panel feels authentic. Once the model is shaped, we fine-tune every detail, from bolts to textures, and then optimize it to keep the game running smoothly. 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/257495ae8065edb270d7183d491a54a3494fbb80.gif

The time needed to model a part can vary. Simple parts might take a few hours, while complex ones can require up to two weeks. We balance accuracy and performance, relying on detailed references to ensure our models look and feel true to life. Many of our artists have spent time working with real car components, so they have a good sense of what details matter the most. Their mechanical experience adds an extra layer of authenticity to the game.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/fd79843d03aa82751d3dd1fdf19d7c6c03c82121.gif


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/69c6d1d8106cf6e2c3fd662b2d49a2d76968d2bf.png

Modeling challenging parts like engine blocks requires a blend of creativity and precision. These components are filled with tiny details that must look accurate while keeping the game running smoothly. To achieve this, we often use techniques like normal mapping, which allows us to create detailed textures without straining performance. Our team’s hands-on experience with real car parts helps us make informed choices, ensuring our models not only look good but also function correctly in-game.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/2ddafe3c747abdb06d82393ed9c6244320508896.gif

Our workflow has evolved to make the process more efficient. We now use shared materials for texturing, making updates quicker, and keeping everything consistent. We’ve also refined our optimization techniques, allowing us to deliver stunning visuals without sacrificing performance. Each new model we create builds on the lessons we've learned, helping us reach higher standards of quality.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/1970ef5fa1d2673afdd3a3ae06969a9db0d2cfcf.gif


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/fc13bf3b0eff446fe35112a8a7add511ec1d2710.png

Creating realistic and engaging car parts is an ongoing journey for our team. We’re constantly refining our techniques, learning from each model we create, and pushing the limits of what’s possible in the Rally Mechanic Simulator. Your feedback is crucial to us, and every suggestion helps us improve and bring you the best experience possible. We can’t wait to share more about our process, new features, and exciting updates we have in store. Stay tuned for more insights into the making of the game, and as always, we’d love to hear what you think! Join the conversation in the comments below or on our Discord. Thank you for being a part of this journey, and see you in the garage!

How to get and install these parts

The game is going to feature a parts shop that you have already seen in the demo. In the upcoming versions of the game, the shop will be expanded compared to the currently available one. This could be said about the entirety of Rally Mechanic Simulator, but let’s not get sidetracked. Let’s say that you’ve just bought a new cool body parts. What you should do next? No need for anything too fancy - just walk up to the car, remove the old body panels and install the new ones. As simple as it gets! We also do realize some of the cars that we used as inspiration for the vehicles in the game have overly complex ways of installing body panels, but we didn’t replicate them. Who’d want to dismantle half of their car to install a side skirt, after all?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/c4d75425759f972a550c2168cb5a9898709479d3.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/9d8527f0c202c9b0d8f13433dcb3eae128f5d94b.png
The performance aspect

Will the body parts influence the performance of the car? No, they won’t. Sure, they would do so in real life, especially considering things like weight, aerodynamics and cooling. At this point in time, though, we want to keep modification of bodywork a simple endeavor that will serve only the aesthetic purpose.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/9d8527f0c202c9b0d8f13433dcb3eae128f5d94b.png
Go (almost) full Picasso

Another huge part of modifying the way a car looks is painting. This will be made available in Rally Mechanic Simulator as well. In the beginning, it will be just a painting area you’ll need to unlock. The capabilities will also be limited - one colour paint for the entire body. It is still pretty cool as most cars you’ve ever seen. Also, as sports cars often have decals and liveries, they are expected to make it into the game at some point in the future. Just imagine the possibilities!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/3ac19a118132434d6b73ff95184052539d095dfc.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/9d8527f0c202c9b0d8f13433dcb3eae128f5d94b.png

This is it for today. We have some massive things in the works, so you can expect big news coming in the near future. Keep an eye out for them!

11.01 - The Start
We’ll make the public playtest build available to the public. All of the people who have requested access to the test should have it granted. The game will most likely be up for at least a few days.

notes.content:
Hello fellow mechanic!

This year has been a wild ride for us. Rally Mechanic Simulator has taken a tangible form and you’ll soon be able to give it a shot during the upcoming playtests. However, it was a busy year for us - we’ve done so much work on the game, we were almost surprised when we were preparing the list of our accomplishments. We’ll present it below and, what’s more interesting, we’ll share our plans for the future.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/9d8527f0c202c9b0d8f13433dcb3eae128f5d94b.png

What was done this year


 Entire gameplay loop - choosing a rally, taking part in it, working in the garage.
 Car upgrade system.
 In-game parts store.
 Car customization system.
 Bodywork damage system.
 The commentary system - you’ll hear it on the radio during the rallies.
 Introduction of parts and assets like garage upgrades that will allow you to progress in the game.
 Plenty of other stuff.


We’ve also made plenty of great art and assets, some of which you can have a look at now!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/328978097ab95bf3d1c0b2b5455600ab66b29620.png

All of this is absolutely necessary for the game to be fun and work well. There are still quite a lot of things we need to make and milestones we have to reach. However, we’re able to say with confidence that this was a good year for the team and we’re close to three next big steps. Let’s talk about the future, then.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/9d8527f0c202c9b0d8f13433dcb3eae128f5d94b.png

2024 is going to be great!

There will be plenty of opportunities to give Rally Mechanic Simulator a shot in the upcoming few months. 

Firstly, there are the upcoming playtests. We’re still working on the game, trying to polish it and to have it in the state we want it to be. The tests are of great importance to us, as we’d love you to enjoy the game and provide feedback regarding it - suggestions, bugs, ideas, and anything goes. The tests will most likely last for a fixed amount of time, so if you wanna give RMS a shot and share your thoughts on the game, you better not miss out on it! The tests will feature the garage and two rallies with a service park at your disposal. The rallies will differ from each other to show a substantial glimpse of what to expect from the game.

Secondly, we expect to release a demo for the upcoming Steam Next Fest in February. It will not be time-limited like the test and will remain up indefinitely. It will definitely be a more extensive build of the game and we’re sure you’ll love it. You’ll be able to play in about 2 months! The demo will feature a couple of hours' worth of gameplay, so you’ll definitely scratch your itch until the next release… :) 

Thirdly, and this is the really big one, we’ll release the Early Access version of Rally Mechanic Simulator around the middle of 2024! You’ll be able to purchase and play the game, while we’ll be delivering and polishing more and more stuff. This will lead to a full release in the future. We really hope for your support from day one!

To finish it off, here’s a statement from the dev team:
We’re extremely happy that we’re able to show you the effect of our hard work in the upcoming weeks and months. We really hope that you’ll take part in creating Rally Mechanic Simulator with us, so we ask you to share each piece of feedback, problem and suggestion you may have. Our ultimate goal is to create a game that will bring fun and joy to both you and us!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/9d8527f0c202c9b0d8f13433dcb3eae128f5d94b.png

That’s all for this entry. So, 2023 was good. But 2024 is going to be absolutely massive for Rally Mechanic Simulator with the upcoming releases. Keep an eye out on our social media and Steam page to follow the upcoming releases. You can also join our Discord server and share your ideas on what to introduce to the game. Cheers!

notes.title: Devlog #7 - Garage
notes.content:
Hi!

Your garage will be the place where the magic happens. Well, not exactly magic, but you’ll be spending a lot of time there doing all sorts of cool stuff, like fixing, painting and tuning your cars. It will be your base of operations. Let’s talk a bit about the garage itself.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/b4cc2e6d9e0105fb38b7da38e4fde43bbc4a3396.png

Creme de la creme
The garage will be the place where you will spend all of your time between rallies. And it will be a time well spent. You will, of course, work on your cars, but there will be so much more to tinker with. Firstly, you’ll be able to modify the garage itself - this involves getting and placing new equipment and facilities, like a painting area or a dyno. They will allow you to work even more thoroughly on your vehicles, all in order to get the best performance. Some of the other facilities that will be at your disposal will include separate working stations for fixing separate car parts, such as transmissions or rims. The more you progress, the more complex fixes you’ll be able to make.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/528764aec326b4270845a316917c03f0cec4867c.jpg

The other important activity in the garage will include the racing team management aspect. Assigning jobs, managing the workforce and so on. Great race drivers and great cars are only a part of an equation when it comes to building a rally force to be reckoned with. And building a great team will be one of your responsibilities.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/4d2daf292e9c3905319d1cd9208b2d5a9f877f32.gif

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/b4cc2e6d9e0105fb38b7da38e4fde43bbc4a3396.png

Decorations
When it comes to the gameplay, we expect that you’ll spend approximately 60% of your time in-game in the garage in the career mode. That’s why there will also be an option to install some decorations to make this space more pleasing. It’s possible that we’ll include other options in the cosmetics department

Navigation
Navigating the garage will be easy and intuitive. You’ll be able to walk there, just like in the case of Motorcycle Mechanic Simulator and approach different workstations. When it comes to accessing a shop to buy more car parts and such, you can easily access these (and other) screens after a simple right mouse button click.

We hope that the garage will be a place you’ll enjoy being at and doing all of the fixing, painting and management. Have a good one, till the next time.

By the way, we’re still working on providing a test build. It’s looking well so far and we hope to release it sometime in the near future :)

notes.title: Devlog #6 - Mechanics
notes.content:
Quite obviously, Rally Mechanic Simulator has “Mechanic” in the name. And you’ll be spending a lot of time dealing with just that. Let’s have a look at the most crucial part of our upcoming game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/8c8f4838b6eaf57d57789c7b872ba2f7b7d29d6c.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/9d8527f0c202c9b0d8f13433dcb3eae128f5d94b.png

Modifications

As we mentioned in an earlier entry in our devlog series, you’ll be able to swap part of your car. The game will belong to the simulation genre, so we’d like to be as accurate in this manner as possible. The parts that could be considered mechanical and will be switchable will include pretty much anything besides the chassis. This includes, but is not limited to:

 Wheels. 
 Brakes.
 Engine components.
 Suspension.
 The drivetrain.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/e9d972ef874534ebd16c6c0e5a63f8d2c3aa182d.gif

However, your role will not be limited to just swapping and fixing parts and keeping your fingers crossed during a rally. You will be responsible for tweaking the performance of the vehicle. One way of going around it would be to install aftermarket parts, and adjust and tune them - trying to balance the reliability and the improved driving characteristics.

An important factor that will have to be considered is what the part will be good for. Some hardware will be made for loose gravelly rallies, some for tarmac and so on. As you can see, setting up the car will have several factors you’ll have to consider. The game aims to not only allow you to be a mechanic - your actions will have a very clear effect on the performance. You’ll be, in this regard, responsible for the race itself.

We don’t expect to feature a full-blown aerodynamics model in the game. However, modification of the body could influence the vehicle’s performance - simply by influencing its weight.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/faaac08eb87b4ed9b60d7ceebad2223937d20d14.gif
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/9d8527f0c202c9b0d8f13433dcb3eae128f5d94b.png

Repairs

As we’ve mentioned earlier, cars get damaged during rallies. You’ll, over time, be forced to fix or swap them. Swaps are straightforward, so let’s talk a bit about fixing them. Each broken part will be taken to an assorted table, where a minigame will be played. During this little bit, you’ll be able to refurbish the part. Of course, at first, the part will need to be dismounted and mounted later. Some parts will not be repairable, such as the car battery or fuses and a replacement will be a must. If you neglect to repair, ultimately, the part’s condition will be marked as 0% and will only be good for selling as scrap.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/14c0163bc1a74f92efd79948da0898a15fd32dd2.gif
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/9d8527f0c202c9b0d8f13433dcb3eae128f5d94b.png

Compatibility

What we haven’t mentioned is the compatibility of car parts. As in the real world, some parts will fit most if not all of the vehicles. However, some parts will be only usable in a narrow assortment of cars. Say, pistons. Of course, each engine has a piston dedicated to it. We won’t go as far as that. However, aftermarket pistons will only be usable in engines with the same layout. For example, in-line pistons (working “vertically”) will not be any good for boxer engines (working “horizontally”).

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/8105ff6b2966e77893b87792065cc742a9b46bc3.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/9d8527f0c202c9b0d8f13433dcb3eae128f5d94b.png

Electronics

Another feature that sets this game apart from other vehicle mechanic simulation games is the possibility of working on the electronics. We’ll definitely cover this topic in the future, so just some small tidbits for today:

 A car with damaged electronics will not be driveable.
 You’ll be allowed to change electronic parts to new and used ones, but you will also be able to fix them like all the other parts.
 Electronics won’t differ wildly between cars and won’t have a huge impact on the performance of the vehicles.


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/47723dc721ae6068d3e349ce91214eee318c89d0.png

That’s all for today. Thanks for reading and see you soon! :)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/9d8527f0c202c9b0d8f13433dcb3eae128f5d94b.png

notes.title: Devlog #5 - Repairing
notes.content:
Where there is damage, there also must be fixes. This is how rallying works. As we talked about the prior in the last devlog, it’s time for the latter. And you’ll be spending a lot of time doing just that. Getting your (virtual hand dirty and making your team’s car run as well as possible. Let’s move on to some details, shall we?

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/b4cc2e6d9e0105fb38b7da38e4fde43bbc4a3396.png
In-game mechanics
There will be a number of ways to repair the damage. Major of them are:
Changing the part to a new one if we took the car to our tent in the service park or if we bought the new part in the store via our garage.

 Fixing the parts in separate workstations. The workstations, due to their cumbersome nature, will have two forms - the basic one, available in the service park and the full one, present in the garage. The garage will also present some exclusive methods of fixing.
 Replacing a particular part when you work on a set of parts.


What does it mean in practice? We analysed how fixing parts worked in our previous game, Motorcycle Mechanic Simulator, took the best ideas and added a slew of new ones. So, you can expect a lot of tinkering with screws, painting, connecting and disconnecting electronics, removing and attaching parts to the car and so on. All of this will be as user-friendly and enjoyable as fixing a battered rally car can get.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/b4cc2e6d9e0105fb38b7da38e4fde43bbc4a3396.png
Getting around to it
One of the most important parts of getting your car race-ready will be identifying damaged parts. Then, you’ll need to figure out what is going to get fixed… And what will have to wait. In the garage, you’ll have all the time in the world. Rebuilding a car from scratch would take something like 40 minutes. However, you will have time limits during rallies. Time’s a limited amount of time in real life and we aim to emulate it. You can expect 5-15 minutes of time to make the car ready to go somehow. You’ll be able to cross the imposed limits, but it will result in a penalty.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/a5b4a18ac989f8cd365c3e5e9c5125e60fca326f.gif

When dealing with more serious damage and restoring parts, you’ll have to schedule that to be done in the garage. You won’t be able to, say, rebuild a transmission or get your rims unbent during a rally - just like in real life. The best, but also costly, way of going around it would be to have spare parts. It all depends on the money. If you have enough funds won in races - no problem. If not, and you probably won’t for a while, then you’re in a pickle. There will also be other avenues for earning, so don’t worry (too overly) about it.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/0b7a766d2aca058ffc4999486c3f0f4ea8b658e8.jpg

There’s this mechanic in the game that we currently call “the danger limit”. You’ll be able to release a car that’s not entirely fixed, but if the danger limit’s broken, you won’t be allowed to partake in the next race. This provides another layer of strategic complexity and a challenge to tackle.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/b4cc2e6d9e0105fb38b7da38e4fde43bbc4a3396.png
Real life vs the game
As Rally Mechanic Simulator is, obviously, a simulator, it’s heavily inspired by real-life know-how. However, we need to make the game fun. And, honestly, there’s a lot of mundanity to the process. So, we decided to take the most boring parts away and “hide” them behind fun minigames. It’s all done in order to make a more playable and enjoyable game and we believe it’s the right call to make.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/f0e481ad109836fe5fe859d8700c7306046b2219.gif

While we may slightly deviate from accuracy in the aforementioned aspect, we want to be as accurate as it gets in terms of presentation. All of the audio and graphic assets will be realistic and there’s a ton of work we’ve already done (and still have to do) to deliver that. One of the things scheduled to be done is to make the aftermath of fixes actually visible on salvaged and restored parts.

An interesting aspect is… Washing the car. It’s a factor in the real world, too.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/173959f0cd0fefba45887520ddaec31d69b9dc70.gif

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/b4cc2e6d9e0105fb38b7da38e4fde43bbc4a3396.png
There will be tuning
Everyone looks fondly at the old games that allowed you to customise your car and rip on the tarmac. We’re not exactly building that, as you won’t be able to drive the car or fit neons under it and audio in the booth. Still, some forms of modification and tuning will be present in the game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/eddab7a816f8ceb4619f56933c3c3e69d1eb6c08.jpg

As per aftermarket body parts, you will be able to modify how the car looks. It probably won’t have an awful lot of influence on performance (if any), but you’ll be able to turn the visuals of your car into something that screams “It’s a purpose-built machine and it’s mean”. By this, we mean that some parts like bumpers and spoilers will be swappable. Additionally, there will be an ability to paint and slap sponsor stickers onto the vehicle.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/11a834d5284aa25b56475cea3c416221c6298cc4.gif

The next thing is mechanical modifications. Let’s be honest - pretty much nobody runs stock cars in rallies. You’ll have a slew of performance parts at your disposal (for the right price). The investment may be sensible - the more money you put into your car, the faster it will be, and the higher your place in the standings will be, so you’ll have money for better parts yatta yatta yatta.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/b4cc2e6d9e0105fb38b7da38e4fde43bbc4a3396.png

Conclusion
As you can see, the repairing work that you’ll encounter will invest you in many levels. From battling against time constraints through prioritising crucial fixes to dealing with limited equipment at times - all with budget management and performance undertones. Simply put, we’re already proud. It’s gonna bun fun, engaging and challenging at once. How will you fare in that environment? We’ll do our best to make Rally Mechanic Simulator as good as it gets and hopefully, you’ll appreciate it!

notes.title: Devlog #4 - Damage
notes.content:
Cars, unfortunately, aren’t indestructible. Whether we talk about wear and tear or massive crashes, you’ll sooner or later find yourself in a mechanic’s shop. Of course, the world of rallying is full of such blunders and they are a vital part of the sport. In this devlog we’ll talk about the damage model present in Rally Mechanic Simulator. After all, it will be your job to sort the cars out and have them ready for the next outing.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/f2f7667f7e2509875ed2433b9420d1fa290a8a4c.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/61c812bebcb4a085afe600917abb82d6d21fc719.gif

How does the damage happen?
Your team’s car accumulates wear and damage during the special stages of the rally. We don’t want to get too much into details, but it will all rack up. What we will say, though is that below a certain threshold of wear, the parts will have an increased chance of failure. When a certain part goes to town, connected parts will also have a chance of being damaged or rendered useless. As many things in cars are interconnected, it just made sense. As an owner of an old French car, I’m well aware of that.

Aside from that, there are also random events. Let’s say that your team’s car hit a tree with its side. You know, that’s the stuff that happens often during rallies. Such events will have a chance to happen during special stages and will in big part depend on the wear of parts. There will also be a second type of event that will damage the car and will not be dependent on how well the vehicle is maintained. 

This also isn’t the only time when damage can occur. You can also do that while fixing parts and failing to do a minigame. More on that in a future devlog. However, this will provide more challenges and force you to be more precise - a luxury few can have in the service park.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/f2f7667f7e2509875ed2433b9420d1fa290a8a4c.png

What if you don’t fix the car?
Not finishing a race is an often occurrence in real life. However, we felt that it would be too harsh for the players. Imagine - you do everything according to plan and suddenly your car burns down on the last special stage due to a random event. It wouldn’t be fun, would it? Because of this, the damage will not render the car unviable. On the other hand, the vehicle will become slower and less competitive. And, as you’ll be striving to get more renown and money, it will make fixes a must. Nobody wants to be last, after all.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/f2f7667f7e2509875ed2433b9420d1fa290a8a4c.png

How will the damage look?
Brutal. Let’s talk a bit about details, though. Through the use of fine craftsmanship and technology, the damage will be (mostly) easy to spot and identify. You can be sure that you’ll see stuff like:

 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/9686424b5cadd4d1c44f8c275826ddfe41b01f09.gif
 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/045571c3c369084f29ad03bdf0c82d173d342e61.gif
 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/b188172a26b351158be094b349bad663c8504666.gif
 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/e904b96efc514933e4efbe9095def46ecda5b010.gif
 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/fe1eb681d56a691be72de8b6e4ade8c9a7757800.gif


The methods we use allow us to have the damage look as if it were made by different types of objects. So, if the car hits a tree it will look significantly different compared to a collision between two vehicles and so on. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/318f28134530afab6c357e7ff5942109e1a047cc.png
The research
Our dev team has gone to a number of rallies. We talked extensively about that in our earlier devlog, so let’s just say that the damage and the work of mechanics they’ve seen have been a huge reference material for them. Aside from this in vivo experience, they’ve also watched countless Youtube videos of rally car crashes and mechanics at work. You can never have too much reference material.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/318f28134530afab6c357e7ff5942109e1a047cc.png
Conclusion
The stuff that’s going to happen during the special stages will certainly get under your skin. Who would need mechanics if damage didn’t exist, though? You’ll find yourself in many various scenarios, sometimes being forced to opt for a compromise. Still - we hope that you have what it takes to be a true mechanic. Thus, the next devlog will be about fixing what’s broken!

Thank you for reading. See you next time!

notes.title: Devlog #3 - Service Parks
notes.content:
Hello mechanics!
Service parks are one of the most crucial parts of the rallying infrastructure. We’ll talk about what they are, what happens there, how we did our research on them and how they will be implemented in Rally Mechanic Simulator in today’s devlog.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/2d47725e5ba2d255c2e9c2ae13967f10423de89d.png

What is a service park?
So, to start from the very top - you most likely already know what a service park is. However, as we want everyone to be on the same footing, here’s a small definition. 

A service park is an area on the grounds of a rally. Its purpose is to be a logistics hub and a place where teams can set their tents and work on their vehicles. The area is also often frequented by the press and spectators - they can look at the cars up close and talk to the crews. This also means that sponsors and advertisers can use the spare space to advertise their brands. From our point of view, the part that is the most important is the ability to place your team’s tent/camp, the base of operations. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/f74e1aab7609a6040e7644c0a8dd8e8c4fd90095.gif

Also, as a side note, a service park is a similar term to a paddock in track racing.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/1ee17119d205eb80513b51e4dff1fad0ebc01e82.png

The tent’s where the magic happens
The key part of the park will be the player’s tent. It will contain the tools and appliances so the player will be able to work on the vehicle during the rallies. It will also feature your team’s sponsors’ branding. Likewise, other teams will also be present in the park and will be doing similar tasks to you.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/02a5321c07c83e6a87d15f77126823378a7d002b.gif

We believe that regular players will be spending approximately 50-60% of the time in the service park. However, it will be dependent on the playstyle, so it could be more, it could be less. More on that in the future, as it could branch out into a separate topic. Let’s just say that you will have a degree of freedom when it comes to preparing for the rally and making fixes and modifications to the car.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/1ee17119d205eb80513b51e4dff1fad0ebc01e82.png

We went to rallies to see them in real life 
The “simulator” in the title obliges us to provide a high degree of accuracy to real life. Therefore, we had to do some research on how to create accurate service parks. There are two ways we went about it. The first one is relying on 3rd parties’ content. We scrolled through and watched countless pictures and videos of such parks on the internet. However, feeling that it was not enough, we decided to go a step further. Thus, we sent our team to some actual rallies. so they can have first-hand experience. 

The most prominent trip was to the “Barbórka” rally. It’s a well-known short rally in Poland. Even though it’s not a part of any series, the event is one of the most popular rallies in our country - frequented by professionals, semi-professionals and amateurs. This means that we had an opportunity to see a lot of great specialists and a vast array of cars:

 Various rally versions of Skoda Fabia dominated the event, however, there were also some purpose-built Fords, Hyundais and a Volkswagen and a Citroen that managed to get into the top 10.
 Two legendary cars - Mitsubishi Lancer Evo and Subaru Impreza - had their fair share of representation.
 To the joy of all, RWD cars were also present at the event, the most eye-catching was definitely a 911 GT3.
 Some cars that have been historically associated with rallying, such as Renault Clio Williams, Lancia Delta Integrale HF and Ford Sierra Cosworth were also there.
 Good old FWD and AWD civilian cars with mods could be spotted, like an Audi A3 or a bunch of Civics.
 There were even some oldtimers, such as Lancia Fulvia and Fiat 126p.

The variety of vehicles and degree of professionalism granted us a unique opportunity to see and learn about many different approaches and sides of car servicing during such an event - a huge thank you to all the members of the dev team, who actively learned and documented what we saw there. We’ve also had smaller excursions that supplemented us with even more knowledge. This means that the research done was thorough - we still expect to view more 3rd party materials, and maybe there will also be some expeditions further down the line as well.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/66216344703393a0a111efbcf401480ab73cc489.png
A small disclaimer - we mentioned the cars above to show you that we’ve seen people work on them. This is not a declaration that cars made after them will be featured in the game. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/1ee17119d205eb80513b51e4dff1fad0ebc01e82.png

The implementation and accuracy
How will this knowledge be implemented in Rally Mechanic Simulator? Looking at service parks as a whole, we realised that there’s a specific vibe about them and we did our best to replicate it. The game is going to be the most accurate in how the tents look - not surprising, considering that you’ll spend a lot of time there. However, we also designed the tents of other teams in high detail.

The next thing that’s always striking there are the advertisements and sponsor branding, so we decided to deliver a proper experience in this regard as well. At this point in time, we still think about how to implement visitors and onlookers into the game, as they will not be crucial and could pose some problems in terms of the game performance - we’ll see how it goes with them. Parks will also differ from each rally to another - as they do in real life - and you, as the player will be able to modify and expand the tent during the game’s progression. That sounds like a topic for the future, though, doesn’t it?

To further enhance the immersion, we decided to put a lot of emphasis on the sounds. All the chatter, the clank of tools and the howling winds certainly add to the experience. They alone could make you feel like you were in the middle of a busy service park.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/7ee675b0a81b3dc155e9f4d221a6240b3c0d217d.gif

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/1ee17119d205eb80513b51e4dff1fad0ebc01e82.png

Conclusion
To wrap it up, here are some bullet points:

 A service park is an area where all the mechanical work and logistics go on during rallies.
 It’s in big part composed of tents where rally teams work on their vehicles.
 You’ll spend a huge part of the game in said parks.
 We’ve done a lot of research regarding service parks, including travels to rallies.
 The game will be quite accurate when it comes to the portrayal of service parks with a slight degree of customizability; it’s still being worked on.


So, how do you feel about that? We’re sure you’d already want to give it a shot. More articles about the game are coming soon and we’re working hard, so keep your fingers crossed!

Cheers and see you next time (soon)!

notes.title: Devlog #2
notes.content:
Hey there, Mechanics!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/287ea62b0a9b6630e759844ad52a26c0dda83888.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/9c241107deeba51de9186bb2b8fe8317ff9990e8.gif
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/318f28134530afab6c357e7ff5942109e1a047cc.png
Now, let's talk about the parts. We've got a whole set of them for you to play with. During the game, you'll be able to put on or take off parts in bigger sets like the brake set, giving you an edge and saving some precious time.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/541db00a51ff348b96225eb7c959fa87cf6dec2c.gif
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/318f28134530afab6c357e7ff5942109e1a047cc.png

But here's the game changer—the wiring system. We've gone all out in paying attention to this detail. It's not just about the electrical system, though. We've got functioning piping and connections for fluids and air. It's all about creating a realistic experience!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40282246/318f28134530afab6c357e7ff5942109e1a047cc.png

That's all for today, folks. We're diving back into work, so get ready to get your hands dirty.
We know that graphics and gifs won't give you the feeling of the game, so you can start getting ready for the demo. We will provide more info soon!!! Stay tuned!

And hey, if you want to chat, drop by our Discord and say hi. Give us a high five!

Hi Mechanics!

We are ready to start sharing information with you about our game. In the coming weeks, we will share some insight about different development parts. And the culmination will be the demo.

For starters, we would like to show you the car editing tool. With it, developers and modders will be able to configure cars and details in many ways.
